title: Performance Lab
description: Write up experiments with numbers, graphs, and explanations:
hints: All three are about the cache and the branch predictor (lesson 13.04): memory is fetched in 64-byte lines, so reading neighbours is nearly free and jumping around is not; a branch that goes the same way each time is predicted almost perfectly.
Make sure the compiler cannot throw the work away: print the sum at the end of each experiment.
requirements: Three timed experiments, each in Release with `std::chrono::steady_clock`, repeated 5 times with the best time kept:
adding up a 4,000 × 4,000 grid row by row, then column by column
an array of structs vs a struct of arrays when only one field is used
summing values over 128 in sorted and unsorted data
For each, a comment with your times and a sentence explaining them
